name: Azure Authentication (az / Az PowerShell / Mg Graph)
description: Authenticate to Azure/Entra as a compromised user or service principal across the three CLIs: az (cross-platform, ARM), Az PowerShell (ARM), and Microsoft Graph PowerShell (Entra ID). Supports password, client-secret/cert, and access-token flows.
source: MCRTA (CyberWarFare Labs) - Multi-Cloud Red Team Analyst: Azure

examples.label: az - get an ARM access token

notes: Three planes: az / Az PowerShell target ARM (management.azure.com); Mg Graph targets Entra ID (graph.microsoft.com) - you often need BOTH (a token for one resource does not work on the other). For -ServicePrincipal $cred: Username = Application (Client) ID, Password = client secret. Long-term creds = user pw / SSO pw / client id+secret/cert; short-term = OAuth access token. Grab an ARM token with 'az account get-access-token' and reuse it via Connect-AzAccount -AccessToken.

defense.why_it_works: Azure exposes the same identities through multiple credential types (passwords, service-principal secrets/certs, OAuth access tokens) across ARM and Microsoft Graph. Any valid credential - including a stolen access token - grants API access at the identity's assigned RBAC/directory-role scope, with no host foothold required.
defense.prerequisites: A valid credential: user password, service-principal app id + secret/cert, or an OAuth access token for management.azure.com or graph.microsoft.com.
defense.impact: T1078.004 Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts. API access to Azure/Entra at the principal's privilege - the entry point for all further cloud enumeration and attack.
defense.detection: Entra sign-in logs: interactive vs non-interactive / service-principal sign-ins, new/unusual IPs, ROPC / device-code flows, impossible travel. Azure Activity Log for token use.
defense.artifacts: Entra ID SignInLogs (UPN/appId, IP, clientAppUsed), Azure Activity Log, token issuance events.
defense.prevention: Conditional Access (MFA, block legacy/ROPC, device compliance, named locations). Least-privilege RBAC + Entra roles. Short-lived credentials; rotate SP secrets; prefer managed identities/certs over secrets.
defense.evasion: Use tokens (no interactive sign-in), authenticate from an allowed IP/region, and reuse a legitimate service principal to blend with normal automation.
defense.misconfiguration: No Conditional Access / MFA; long-lived service-principal secrets; over-privileged users/SPs.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# SP with a long-lived secret and Contributor at subscription scope, no CA/MFA:
az login --service-principal -u <app_id> -p <secret> --tenant <tid>   # succeeds from anywhere
defense.secure_config:
# Enforce Conditional Access + MFA; block ROPC/legacy auth.
# Use managed identities or cert-based SP auth; rotate secrets; scope RBAC to least privilege.
